header.title: AnimatedNumber
header.description: Animates changes to a number: counters, balances, prices and metrics. By default (`effect="count"`) it interpolates the value frame by frame; with `fade`, `up` or `down` it swaps the formatted figure with a crossfade or a short slide. Pass the value in `value` and format it with `Intl.NumberFormat` (`locales`, `formatOptions`) or your own `format` function.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine props, change the value with the buttons and check the generated code. Increases use the `enter` timing and decreases use `exit`.
playground.label: Balance

base.title: Basic counter
base.description: With the defaults the number interpolates over `500` ms: increases use the `standard` easing and decreases use `exit`. The root is a `span` with tabular numbers, so you can drop it inside text. When `value` is an integer, intermediate steps are integers too.

effects.title: Effects
effects.description: `count` walks through the intermediate values. `fade` crossfades the old and new figure at the same time; `up` adds an upward slide (the new figure enters from below) and `down` does the opposite. The direction comes from the effect, not from whether the value rises or falls. These three only animate when the formatted text changes.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: `formatOptions` goes to `Intl.NumberFormat` together with `locales`. `duration` and `easing` accept `{ enter, exit }`: here increases take `620` ms with `emphasized` and decreases `420` ms with `exit`.

percent.title: Percent
percent.description: With `style: "percent"`, `value` goes from `0` to `1`: `0.42` renders as `42%`. `maximumFractionDigits` applies to the displayed percent, not the raw value, and the count keeps enough decimals so intermediate steps do not jump.

format.title: Custom format, prefix and suffix
format.description: `format` receives the interpolated value on every frame (with `count`) or the final value (with `fade`, `up` or `down`) and returns the text; when you pass it, `locales` and `formatOptions` are ignored. `prefix` and `suffix` render before and after the figure, outside the animation.

round.title: Count decimals (round)
round.description: `round` sets how many decimals the intermediate count values have, overriding the precision inferred from `value` and `formatOptions`. It is clamped to `0`–`20` and only applies to `effect="count"`. Here the same value with `2` and `4` decimals.

trend.title: Trend color (trendClassName)
trend.description: `trendClassName` adds the `up` class to the root when the value rises and `down` when it falls. The last trend sticks until the next change; there is none on mount.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onStart(from)` fires when a change begins, with the value being displayed, and `onComplete(to)` when it settles. `onAnimatedNumber` reports that the animation started (`reason: "enter"`) and `outAnimatedNumber` that it ended (`exit`), was disabled (`disabled`) or unmounted (`unmount`). If the value changes mid-way, `onStart` fires again but `onAnimatedNumber` does not.

disabled.title: Disabled
disabled.description: With `isDisabled` the figure jumps straight to the new value, just like with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. `onStart` and `onComplete` still fire, one right after the other.

asChild.title: No wrapper (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild` the classes, styles and ref go to the single child (a `strong` here) and its content is replaced by the figure. Use it to keep semantics inside a paragraph, a table cell or an `output`. The child must be exactly one element: without one, the number is not rendered.

utilities.title: Utility classes
utilities.description: Classes from `utilities.css` (`gemst-inline-flex`, `gemst-relative`…) go through `classNames` to adjust layout, overflow or position without a design system stylesheet. Here `gemst-inline-flex` goes on `root` and `gemst-relative` on `value`. They are already included in `styles.css`.

header.title: AnimatedNumber API
header.description: Props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types for `AnimatedNumber`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for every effect, format and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemsitions/animated-number` with its `animated-number.css`, or from the root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> (except children) and forwards them to the root span, or to the child with asChild. In that case classes and styles merge with the child's and, when both define the same handler (onClick…), the child's runs first. The component adds aria-busy while it animates.

items.live: The visible figure has aria-hidden. The formatted final value lives in a visually hidden span with aria-live="polite" (.gemst-animated-number__sr), so screen readers announce the result once per change instead of every intermediate frame.
items.busy: While the animation runs, the root has aria-busy.
items.affixes: prefix and suffix sit outside the live region: they are read when browsing the page, but not announced when the value changes. If the unit matters, include it in format or formatOptions (for example style: "currency" or "unit").
items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the figure jumps to the final value. The preference is read on every render, not listened to live: if it changes, it applies on the next value change.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion keeps the animation and adds the gemst-ignore-reduced-motion class to the root. Use it only when motion is essential.
items.tabular: Tabular numbers (tabular-nums) keep the width from jumping while counting. It still changes when the number of digits changes (from 1,000 to 999).
items.asChild: With asChild, pick a child with the right semantics (strong, output, td): its content is replaced by the figure and the live region.

items.root: Root (`span`). `position: relative`, baseline-aligned `inline-flex`, `max-width: 100%`, `color: inherit` and tabular numbers.
items.effect: Active effect. With `fade`, `up` and `down`, `__value` becomes an `inline-grid` with `overflow: hidden` to stack both figures.
items.playing: While the count or the figure swap runs.
items.disabled: Added with `isDisabled`. Figures have no transition.
items.ready: Only with `fade`, `up` and `down`, after mount: enables transitions so the first render does not animate.
items.from: Only with `fade`, `up` and `down`: the frame where the new figure paints at its start pose with transitions off.
items.sr: Visually hidden copy of the final value, with `aria-live="polite"`.
items.slot: Each figure during a `fade`, `up` or `down` swap. Both share the same grid cell and transition `opacity` and `transform`.
items.slotRole: `incoming` uses the `enter-*` variables; `outgoing` uses `exit-*` and ignores pointer events.
items.slotState: `in` is the resting pose (`opacity: 1`); `out` hides it and, with `up` or `down`, shifts it by `--gemst-animated-number-shift`.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Written inline on every render (as `0ms` with `isDisabled` or reduced motion), except `shift`. The count runs in JavaScript: the transition variables are only used by the `fade`, `up` and `down` figures.

items.duration: Duration of the current phase (increase = `enter`, decrease = `exit`). No CSS rule reads it.
items.delay: Delay of the current phase. No CSS rule reads it.
items.easing: Resolved curve of the current phase. No CSS rule reads it.
items.enterDuration: Transition duration of the incoming figure. Default `500ms`.
items.exitDuration: Transition duration of the outgoing figure. Default `500ms`.
items.enterDelay: Delay of the incoming figure. Default `0ms`.
items.exitDelay: Delay of the outgoing figure. Default `0ms`.
items.enterEasing: Curve of the incoming figure. Default `standard`.
items.exitEasing: Curve of the outgoing figure. Default `exit`.
items.shift: Slide distance for `up` and `down`. Default `0.4em`. Not written inline: override it with a class or `style`.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global gemsitions variables the CSS uses as defaults.

items.easingStandard: Default for `--gemst-animated-number-easing` and `--gemst-animated-number-enter-easing`. The component writes the resolved curve inline, so redefining the token does not change the animation: use `easing`.
items.easingExit: Default for `--gemst-animated-number-exit-easing`, with the same caveat.

props.title: Props
props.description: `value` is required; everything else is optional.

content.title: Content
content.description: The value to display, what surrounds it and where it mounts.

format.title: Format
format.description: How the number becomes text and how many decimals the count uses.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: In milliseconds. `enter` applies to increases (or the incoming figure) and `exit` to decreases (or the outgoing one).

state.title: State
state.description: How the animation is turned off.

items.value: Target value. Non-finite values (`NaN`, `Infinity`) are treated as `0`.
items.prefix: Content before the figure. It is not animated and not part of the live region.
items.suffix: Content after the figure. It is not animated and not part of the live region.
items.children: Only with `asChild`: the element used as root. Its content is replaced by the figure. Ignored without `asChild`.
items.asChild: Applies classes, styles and ref to the single child instead of a `span`. Without exactly one child element, the number is not rendered.
items.locales: `Intl.NumberFormat` locales. Ignored when `format` is set. Must be stable across renders.
items.formatOptions: `Intl.NumberFormat` options. Ignored when `format` is set. Pass a stable object: a new one on every render restarts the count. With `style: "percent"`, decimals apply to the displayed percent.
items.format: Function that turns the number into text. Receives the interpolated value on every frame (`count`) or the final one (`fade`, `up`, `down`).
items.round: Decimals for intermediate count values. Overrides the inferred precision. Clamped to `0`–`20`; only with `count`.
items.effect: `count` interpolates the number; `fade` crossfades figures; `up` and `down` add a vertical slide.
items.trendClassName: Classes added to the root based on the last change: `up` when it rose, `down` when it fell.
items.duration: Duration. With `count`, `enter` is for increases and `exit` for decreases; with `fade`, `up` and `down`, for the incoming and outgoing figure.
items.delay: Wait before starting. Accepts `{ enter, exit }` like `duration`.
items.easing: Token (`standard`, `enter`, `exit`, `emphasized`, `linear`), a `cubic-bezier(...)` or `{ enter, exit }`. With `count`, any CSS curve other than `cubic-bezier` is treated as linear.
items.isDisabled: Jumps straight to the new value, without animation. Turning it on mid-way sends `disabled` to `outAnimatedNumber`.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Animates even when the user prefers reduced motion. Only when essential.
items.onStart: Fires when a change begins, with the value being displayed.
items.onComplete: Fires when the figure reaches the final value. With `isDisabled` or reduced motion, right after `onStart`.
items.onAnimatedNumber: Fires when the animation starts (`reason: "enter"`). Does not fire when motion is off.
items.outAnimatedNumber: Fires when it ends (`exit`), is disabled mid-way (`disabled`) or unmounts while animating (`unmount`).
items.style: Inline styles for the root. Merged with the `--gemst-animated-number-*` variables, which take precedence.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `span`, or the child with `asChild`).
